newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Sterling sizes up key 2.8080 marks hurdle.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Sterling sizes up key 2.8080 marks hurdle.

text.p: Sterling has established an ever firmer footing above 2.78 marks but now faces major resistance around 2.8080, chart watchers said.
The 2.8080 zone represents a 78.6 percent Fibonacci retracement of the pound's downmove from the 2.8330 high reached on May 6 to the recent low of 2.7240.
Though this could rebuff the pound at its first attempt, analysts said channel and Elliott support around 2.7750-20 should eventually provide the launchpad for a move higher.
Sterling was quoted at 2.7855/65 marks at 0733 GMT, up from late Wednesday's European level of 2.7720/30.
"It is expected to hold the 2.7750/20 support and from here it should move impulsively higher," said Hans-Guenter Redeker, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank in London.
Cable, meantime, is trapped in a range -- though any pressure is to the downside, analysts said.
"As long as $1.6450 caps, sterling is going down," said Francoise Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston here.
Support is at $1.6335, a pivot and former resistance, with a break below there targeting $1.6280, said Skelley.
"Overall we're looking at $1.6060, which is an uptrend," she added.
The pound stood at $1.6350/60 at 0858 GMT compared with $1.6391/96 in late Europe yesterday.
